evaluationContext.purpose: Apply the multidimensional report contract to the immutable commit that introduced the contract, schema, validators, fixture, tests, and program integration.
evaluationContext.evaluator: same-task Codex self-assessment with deterministic repository checks
evaluationContext.method: Git object binding, schema validation, negative controls, acceptance-map reconciliation, and repository-wide verification
evaluationContext.claimScope: The eight-file evaluation core and its bb65a26 integration only; not the whole Harness, another repository, a live Agent, or an admitted standard.

evidence.source: git ls-tree -r bb65a26c3e0c73c925e761c09da06e44b76cbad3 over the eight evaluation-core paths
evidence.scope: Eight Git blobs; full git ls-tree records sorted lexicographically, joined with UTF-8 LF, and no terminal newline; manifest SHA-256 9a9772709ee72753af6bdec9fc0eb6224444192a13cb2abd52c48e60c7db0289.
limitations: Git identity proves exact bytes and history, not semantic quality or value.

evidence.scope: Contract vocabulary, source anchors, acceptance links, schema fields, evidence references, uncertainty, floor coverage, and accepted-status guards.
limitations: The validators encode the same contract they assess and require independent review for external validity.

evidence.scope: Positive fixtures and negative mutations for score injection, missing dimensions, evidence drift, Skill-necessity overclaim, hard-standard promotion, and false accepted status.
limitations: Unit tests do not establish usability, cross-host interpretation, domain fitness, or longitudinal maintenance.

evidence.source: python -B scripts/verify.py at bb65a26 and immediate post-change reruns
evidence.scope: Repository-required files, program topology, acceptance inventory, prior validators, and new evaluation validators.
limitations: A local verifier pass is not remote CI, independent acceptance, release readiness, or product value.

evidence.scope: 61 acceptance criteria remain 44 verified, 16 partial, and 1 planned; this package changes no assessment authority.
limitations: The map is repository governance evidence, not external acceptance.

evidence.scope: Current official lifecycle, product quality, quality in use, evaluation process, secure development, supply-chain, delivery, productivity, and AI-risk locators with bounded uses and limitations.
limitations: Some standards are paywalled, one is under review, AI RMF 1.0 is under revision, and locators are not content-hash pins.

evidence.source: Git HEAD and origin/main read-only snapshot after push
evidence.scope: main and origin/main both resolved to bb65a26c3e0c73c925e761c09da06e44b76cbad3 with ahead/behind 0/0.
limitations: Remote synchronization does not prove CI, release, review, or runtime behavior.

unknowns: No real project team has yet used the report contract to make an engineering decision.
limitations: Repository alignment is stronger than demonstrated user or organizational value.

unknowns: Cross-thread and cross-host interpretation of the evaluation vocabulary remains untested.
limitations: The same implementation authored the contract and its fidelity checks.

unknowns: No independent architecture review has challenged the five-layer separation.
limitations: Coherent static layering is not proof that later adapters and profiles will remain decoupled.

unknowns: Mutation depth, property-based coverage, and long-term schema migration behavior remain unmeasured.
limitations: The implementation is small and deterministic but has not received independent code review.

unknowns: No dedicated independent security, privacy, threat, or misuse review was performed.
limitations: No executable third-party payload or secret-bearing data was added, but absence of detected risk is not positive assurance.

unknowns: External standard contents are not hash-pinned and future source revisions may change interpretations.
limitations: Git provenance is exact for repository files, while external normative-source provenance remains locator-bound.

unknowns: No rollback drill or remote CI execution was performed.
limitations: Git revert is available and bounded, but availability is not an observed recovery result.

unknowns: Future runtime orchestration based on this contract would require a separate operational profile.
limitations: The evaluated target is a static contract package, not a deployed service.

unknowns: No schema version migration or retirement has yet occurred.
limitations: Separation and fail-closed tests support change, but longitudinal maintenance is absent.

unknowns: No independent reviewer or downstream accountable adopter has signed the report.
limitations: Ownership and authority are explicit in the contract but not externally exercised.

unknowns: The Agent-authored path has no independent per-hop intent-loss ledger for this change.
limitations: Explicit authority boundaries prevent overclaim but do not prove preserved intent or human-control effectiveness.

unknowns: Authoring time, review burden, verifier cost, context cost, and future maintenance cost were not measured.
limitations: No efficiency or resource claim is eligible.

floorResults.disposition: Claims are bound to one immutable commit, exact Git objects, explicit command surfaces, and stated limitations.
The package changes repository research and validation only; it installs no capability and grants no hard-standard, account, runtime, or acceptance authority.
The change is one Git commit with exact identity and a bounded revert path; no rollback success is claimed.

floorResults.owner: repository owner and future acceptance authority
floorResults.disposition: The report remains needs-verification, records no independent review, seeks no acceptance, and preserves all partial or planned program states.

unknownsAndLimitations: This is a same-system self-assessment of the framework that produced it.
No independent human or Agent review, live-domain use, cross-host use, longitudinal maintenance, remote CI, or rollback drill is included.
The report evaluates one immutable change-set and cannot support a whole-repository, product-quality, release-readiness, or hard-standard claim.
counterevidenceAndDisagreements: Deterministic tests show internal consistency but cannot establish external validity or usability.
The source map is broad but some normative texts are paywalled, mutable, under review, or under revision.
An Agent-authored report can preserve explicit uncertainty while still missing tacit human judgment.

nextEvidence: Obtain an independent review of the dimension, floor, evidence, and status judgments.
Apply the same schema to one non-self-referential bounded software change with a different risk profile.
Record review burden and any disagreement rather than converting consensus into a scalar score.
nextEvidenceAndFallback.fallback: Retain this report as a self-assessment and keep the framework research-only if independent review or a suitable second target is unavailable.

revalidationAndRetirementTriggers: The report schema, dimension vocabulary, floor candidates, evidence grades, or authority model changes.
A non-self-referential target exposes a missing dimension, misleading assessment state, or unusable evidence burden.
A mature native, official, or reviewed external framework provides a demonstrably superior carrier.
Independent review identifies a material overclaim, omission, conflict, or anti-gaming weakness.

independentReview.scope: The deterministic checks are not independent judgment.

acceptanceAuthority.owner: repository owner and separately governed standards authority
acceptanceAuthority.scope: No project-wide acceptance, release readiness, CALIBRATION handoff, ASSETS admission, or hard-standard promotion is requested.

claimBoundary: The bb65a26 evaluation package is internally consistent, source-bound, machine-validated, reversible, and honestly non-authoritative; independent validity, real-domain usefulness, cross-host behavior, efficiency, and standard eligibility remain unproved.
